decisions: This repository is independent of build-a-web-page-for-ios.
Hardware target is original ESP32 integrated TWAI plus NXP TJA1051T/3 SO8.
Default runtime state must be passive/listen-only with a hardware-enforced transmitter inhibit.
Version 1 contracts use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and a logical OpenAPI 3.1 host API.
Data-frame payload byte count must match DLC; standard IDs use 11 bits; extended IDs use 29 bits; this contract models Classical CAN only.
A TX request never grants authorization; host-side checks require fresh firmware-originated state and firmware/physical interlock checks remain independent.
Unknown/unsupported diagnostic capabilities remain disabled; validated findings require independent evidence.
Vehicle CAN identifiers, bit rate, topology, and signal mappings remain unknown until supported by evidence.
No official Python API/utility for native Proteus schematic generation was confirmed in local examples or official public resources reviewed; S09 must verify the route rather than invent one.
S01 test results prove contract-layer behavior only, not live CAN, hardware, UI, persistence, simulator, or vehicle compatibility.
S02 source/build foundation compiled for original ESP32 using PlatformIO Core 6.2.0, espressif32 6.9.0 and ESP-IDF 5.3.1.
S02 TWAI controller startup is Listen Only and disabled by default; no hardware transmit API is present in S02.
GPIOs and vehicle bitrate remain unassigned/unconfirmed; the generic esp32dev 4MB profile proves compilation only and is not a physical-board profile.
TX safety policy host tests and source guards pass; the independent physical interlock and physical board have not been bench-tested.
S03 implements bounded TWAI/application queues and explicit software drop/malformed-frame counters; armed TX auto-disarms on application-queue overflow.
Firmware serial telemetry uses CW1-prefixed schema-v1 handshake/device_status/can_frame JSON records; timestamps are monotonic observation times, not hardware SOF or UTC.
The single-frame C TX API is centrally guarded but intentionally not exposed as a serial command; hardware-init, bitrate evidence and TX capability remain disabled by default.
Host-mocked integration validates firmware logic deterministically but is not physical bus, bench interlock, or vehicle evidence.
